messages.subject: Error: Argument burnin (or sample) missing
messages.body_plain:
If one does not explicitly specify the burnin and sample iterations in 0.2-4, then the error in the subject line will likely pop up. This is corrected in the development version and can be avoided by specifying the burnin and sample iterations in the call to bcfa/bsem/blavaan.

Ed

messages.subject: Naive question about cross-loading estimations
messages.body_plain:
(sorry for ma very bad english and for my very naive question)

I began with blavaan. I understood that BSEM introduce priors covariance between cross-loading (cf Muthén B, Asparouhov T , 2012)
I would like to estimate the cross-loading for a CFA model with blavaan
For example
HS.model <- '
visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9
'

I would like to get the estimated covariance of Xi, that is seem possible with BSEM (by posteriors estimations based on priors)

Merkle and Rosseel (blavaan: Bayesian Structural Equation Models via Parameter Expansion) explained that these covariance are built by phantom latent variables.
I don't understand how I can get these covariances estimated in the blavaan results.

In the Bollen example developped by Merkle and Rosseel they specified the residual correlations.
Are we obliged to integrate specifical residual correlations in tje model?
Can we get the residual correlations for all covariances without introduce these in the model?
If not, where is really the difference between lavaan and blavaan?

A very simple and naive question...
Best
Hervé

messages.subject: Re: Naive question about cross-loading estimations
messages.body_plain:
Hervé,

I'm not sure whether this is what you want, but an example of estimating cross-loadings in that model is here:

http://faculty.missouri.edu/~merklee/blavaan/crossload.html

You then ask about an "estimated covariance of Xi" and residual correlations. I think you're asking whether you can automatically estimate all residual covariances in the model? There is no automatic way to do it; you would have to specify them in the model syntax, similarly to the cross-loadings example above.

Also, the user generally does not have to worry about phantom latent variables; the blavaan package automatically converts covariances to phantom latent variables where necessary.

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Naive question about cross-loading estimations
messages.body_plain:
Herve (cc'ing blavaan group),

There is currently not an automatic way to specify all residual covariances. However, you can use R's paste() function to save some typing. I would do something like this:

hsm <-  '

visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

rcovs <- paste(sapply(1:8, function(i) paste0("x", i, " ~~ ", paste0("x", (i+1):9, collapse=" + "))), collapse="\n")

HS.modelTOT <- paste0(hsm, "\n", rcovs)

Ed
